result.title: Self-Indexing Latent Memories for Access-Aware Continual Instruction Tuning of LLMs
result.summary: Continual instruction tuning often preserves old skills with task-private modules. Inference still requires selecting the right module from the prompt alone. We introduce Task-Isolated Latent Adapter Continual Training (TILA-CT), a replay-free method that makes each task module self-indexing. Each task receives a latent memory and adapter bank in a frozen LLM. During adaptation, the memory gathers causal-prefix information and injects task-conditioned context. For access, its persistent state provides the routing prototype used by a shared prompt-only router. On the 8-task CT-Pipeline stream, TILA-CT achieves 65.19 acquisition and 63.98 final macro score, with 1.38 points of average forgetting. A middle-reversed order gives 65.38 acquisition and 64.17 final macro score. Across 6 backbones, final scores remain within 1.5 points of acquisition. Ablations support memory-derived routing keys and causal gathering. Final macro routing accuracy is 93.9\%, and oracle routing recovers 1.21 final macro points. These results separate preserved task computation from learned access to it.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 TILA-CT：在冻结 LLM 中为每个任务配置一套 latent memory 与 adapter bank，训练时由记忆聚合 causal-prefix 信息并注入任务条件上下文，推理时直接以记忆的持久状态作为共享 prompt-only 路由器的路由原型，从而在无回放下实现任务的自我索引与隔离。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用 latent 状态自身充当索引以选择对应模块」的访问机制，可能为 LVR 中 latent 假设、视觉证据或缓存的选取与访问问题提供一条可核查的方法线索；但该文为纯文本、任务隔离设定，迁移可行性尚待确认。
